newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU speeds up biotech maize scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: EU speeds up biotech maize scrutiny.

text.p: European Union scientists are speeding up examination of whether to approve imports of genetically modified maize, European Commission officials said.
"We've asked them to give an opinion urgently," a Commission official said after two days of farm trade talks with U.S. Department of Agriculture officials.
But EU scientific committees on foodstuffs, pesticides and animal nutrition are not expected to reach conclusions until December - that is, after the U.S. maize crop is harvested.
"Scientists tend to take a cautious approach," the official said, adding that U.S. approval procedures were also long.
The Commission said it understood U.S. concern.
"We take it very seriously...it's in danger of becoming a major trade issue," the official added.
U.S. officials said they did not want to push the EU scientists too hard but that a huge trade flow was at risk.
"We are trying to reconcile the two forces," said one official, adding Washington was hopeful a solution could be found.
U.S. maize exports to the EU were worth $530 million in 1995/96 (July/June) when world prices were exceptionally high.
